physical_harm: Injuries inflicted on 'RS' and 'BS', with 'BS' succumbing to injuries
number_of_offences: Eight accused charged, four finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as accused raised lalkara for retribution
motive: Enmity due to daughter being teased
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the injury was caused directly and deep into the stomach of the victim, a very vital part, which led to death within a short time.
witness_credibility: The court relied on the evidence of the complainant and the injured eye witnesses, as well as the medical examination reports, to establish the facts of the case.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 25th March, 1996; Trial judgment: 19.01.2007; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: April 20, 2011
legal_representation: P.N. Puri, Manu Sharma, Sanjay Jain, D.P. Singh, Avneet Toor, Kuldip Singh for the appearing parties
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal of some accused, conviction of others; High Court: Affirmed the trial court's judgment; Supreme Court: Allowed appeal of Sher Singh, dismissed appeals of other accused
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the injury caused to the deceased was directly and deeply inflicted into the stomach, a vital part, leading to death within a short time, and that the accused had a common intention to cause that injury.
defence_argument: The defence argued that even if the prosecution's case was true, the matter would not fall under murder but under culpable homicide not amounting to murder. They also claimed that the injury attributed to Sher Singh could have resulted from a scuffle and not from a lathi, and that the provisions of Section 34 of the IPC were not made out as there was no intention to commit murder.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the question of whether the injury was caused with the intention to cause death is a matter of objective satisfaction of the Court, based on the facts and circumstances of the case.
precedent_relied_upon: Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1958 SC 465; Laxman Karlu Nikalje v. The State of Maharashtra 1968 (3) A SCR 685; Harjinder Singh v. Delhi Administration AIR 1968 SC 867; Randhir Singh alias Dhire v. State of Punjab 1981 (4) SCC 484; Tho'an v. State of Tamil Nadu 1984 (2) SCC 133; Arun Nivalaji More v. State of Maharashtra 2006 (2) SCC 613
